title: Total energy calculation
description: Essential: Student correctly calculates total solar energy converted using Q = 0.2 × E₀ × time × area with proper unit handling.

title: Final temperature determination
description: Essential: Student obtains correct final temperature using t = t₀ + Q/(c·m) with c = 4200 J/(kg·°C) for water.

title: Energy conversion reasoning
description: Important: Student identifies that only 20% of incident solar energy is converted to water's internal energy.

title: Time unit conversion
description: Important: Student converts 4 hours to seconds (14400 s) for consistent SI units in energy calculation.

title: Specific heat application
description: Important: Student applies Q = mcΔt formula correctly to relate energy to temperature change.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: Student verifies all units are consistent (J, m², s, kg, °C) throughout calculations.

title: Significant figures
description: Optional: Student reports answers with appropriate significant figures (3.02×10⁷ J, 56°C).

title: Forgot efficiency factor
description: Pitfall: Student uses 100% instead of 20% efficiency, calculating energy as 5× too large.

title: Time unit error
description: Pitfall: Student uses hours instead of seconds in energy calculation, getting wrong energy by factor of 3600.

title: Specific heat confusion
description: Pitfall: Student uses wrong specific heat value or confuses Q = mcΔt with other heat formulas.
